caption: The drawing depicts an architectural interior with prominent decorative elements. At the top, there are three large arches, each formed by alternating bands of red and light beige with blue accents in a repeating pattern, and small blue marks radiating outward from the arches. Below the central arch is a structure resembling an altar or tomb with an arched top, outlined in red, and featuring a small cross at the apex and a single blue palm frond inside the arch. The interior background features a peach-colored fence with crosses on top of each post, extending horizontally. To the left of the central structure is a circular object that resembles a stylized sunburst or clock with a red outline and a triangular base. The floor consists of a diamond checkerboard pattern in red and white, angled diagonally, occupying the central area, while the lower foreground displays a section of a brown tiled floor. A small signature “FANNY D. BARRIS” appears in the lower right corner. The composition is primarily red, light beige, blue, and brown, with clean lines and stylized, geometric forms.
title: Wall Painting and Baptismal Niche
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
